subject: Cooking
title: Street Food Safety: The Real Numbers
description: A micro-lesson that makes Street Food Safety: The Real Numbers usable.

hook.text: Tourists fear street food illness. Data shows restaurants cause more foodborne illness than street vendors.

buildup.text: WHO studies found that street food in developing countries has comparable safety to restaurant food.

discovery.text: High turnover is the secret — food is cooked fresh and consumed immediately, leaving little time for bacteria.

twist.text: The biggest risk isn't the food itself — it's contaminated water used for washing dishes and hands.

climax.text: Singapore's hawker centers solved this with regulated water, inspections, and hygiene grades displayed publicly.

punchline.text: The safest street food is the busiest stall. Fast turnover beats fancy kitchens.

quiz.question: What is the biggest food safety risk with street food?

details.summary: WHO estimates that 600 million people fall ill from contaminated food annually, but street food is not the primary culprit. Studies show that high-turnover street stalls serving freshly cooked food can be safer than sit-down restaurants with poor cold storage.
details.whyItMatters: Street food safety concerns are often exaggerated and applied with cultural bias. Understanding actual risk factors empowers travelers to make informed choices rather than avoiding street food entirely.
takeaways: High turnover and fresh cooking make busy stalls relatively safe
Temperature abuse and poor storage cause more illness than cooking method
Well-managed street food can be safer than poorly managed restaurants

faq.question: Is street food actually dangerous?
faq.answer: It depends entirely on the vendor, not the format. Busy stalls that cook fresh to order at high temperatures are often safe. Empty stalls with pre-made food sitting at ambient temperature are risky. The same principles apply to restaurants. Watch for high turnover, visible cooking, and clean oil.

faq.question: What should travelers look for when choosing street food?
faq.answer: Choose stalls with long lines — high turnover means fresh food. Watch the cooking temperature — boiling and frying kill pathogens. Avoid raw ingredients washed in local water. Check that the vendor handles money and food with different hands or uses gloves.
